answer: Treat every agent as a vertex in a reputation graph anchored by a small kernel of long-lived, work-proven agents. New identities start in a thin shale layer: they can transact, but only tiny amounts, and only with counterparties who stake reputation on them. Volume grows only through attested, completed work that builds edges toward the kernel. A sybil can spawn a thousand vertices for free, but it cannot fake the costly history of edges into the kernel, so its shale identities stay capped and cheap to ignore.
